# go-modern-new-expression

**Since:** Go 1.26

## Summary

Use new(value) for pointer fields or arguments instead of generic/type-specific pointer helper functions or temporary variables used only for &value.

## Details

new(value) creates a \*T from a value expression.
In struct literals, prefer Field: new(value) for pointer fields over helper calls whose only purpose is returning &value; keep helpers only when they add behavior.

## Examples

### Example 1

### Before

```go
func Pointer[T any](value T) *T {
  return &value
}

cfg := Config{
  Timeout: Pointer(30),
  Debug:   Pointer(true),
}
```

### After

```go
cfg := Config{
  Timeout: new(30),
  Debug:   new(true),
}
```

### Example 2

### Before 2

```go
timeout := 30
debug := true
cfg := Config{
  Timeout: &timeout,
  Debug:   &debug,
}
```

### After 2

```go
cfg := Config{
  Timeout: new(30),
  Debug:   new(true),
}
```
